title: Coefficients pulled back from the point
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a ring object of $\Sh(*_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$, that is, a
condensed ring ([sk-def-sfb-ring-object]). For a scheme $X$, put
$$
\Lambda_X:=p_X^*\Lambda\in\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab),
$$
where $p_X^*$ is the inverse image from the point
([sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point]).

The ring object structure is transported along the strong monoidal functor
$p_X^*$. The unit is $\Z\cong p_X^*\Z\to p_X^*\Lambda$. The multiplication is
$$
p_X^*\Lambda\otimes p_X^*\Lambda\cong p_X^*(\Lambda\otimes\Lambda)\to p_X^*\Lambda .
$$
This makes $\Lambda_X$ a ring object of $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$, and
$\Lambda\mapsto\Lambda_X$ is a functor from ring objects of
$\Sh(*_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ to ring objects of $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$.
If $\Lambda$ is commutative, then so is $\Lambda_X$.

proof.text: Write the given ring object as $(\Lambda,\mu,\eta)$, with multiplication $\mu:\Lambda\otimes\Lambda\to\Lambda$ and unit $\eta:\mathbf Z\to\Lambda$, as in [sk-def-sfb-ring-object]. By part 4 of [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point], $F=p_X^*$ is a strong monoidal braided functor between the indicated categories of abelian sheaves. Denote its tensor and unit comparison isomorphisms by $\delta_{A,B}:FA\otimes FB\to F(A\otimes B)$ and $\epsilon:\mathbf Z\to F\mathbf Z$. Define the underlying coefficient object to be $\Lambda_X=F\Lambda$, its multiplication to be $\mu_X=F\mu\circ\delta_{\Lambda,\Lambda}$, and its unit to be $\eta_X=F\eta\circ\epsilon$. All these maps have the domains and codomains in the statement; no commutativity hypothesis on $\Lambda$ is used.

source.place: definition and proof, first paragraph: strong monoidal pullback and the unit/multiplication

proof.text: Apply part 1 of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-transport] with $\mathcal C=\Sh(*_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$, $\mathcal D=\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$, $F=p_X^*$ and $R=\Lambda$. Its hypotheses hold because the strong monoidal structure of step 1 is in particular lax monoidal. Its displayed formulas are exactly $\mu_X$ and $\eta_X$, so it gives associativity and both unit laws for these actual maps. Thus the object defined in step 1 is a ring object, rather than merely an unspecified ring structure on $F\Lambda$.

source.place: proof, first paragraph: transport of monoid objects and coherence

proof.text: For a morphism of ring objects $a:\Lambda\to\Lambda'$, set $a_X=F(a)$. Part 1 of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-transport] says that this map respects the transported multiplication and unit. Explicitly, naturality of $\delta$ gives $F(a)\circ\mu_X=F(a\circ\mu)\circ\delta_{\Lambda,\Lambda}=F(\mu')\circ\delta_{\Lambda',\Lambda'}\circ(F(a)\otimes F(a))=\mu'_X\circ(F(a)\otimes F(a))$, and $F(a)\circ\eta_X=F(a\circ\eta)\circ\epsilon=\eta'_X$. The identities $F(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$ and $F(b\circ a)=F(b)\circ F(a)$ give the identity and composition laws. This is the claimed functor on ring objects.

source.place: proof, first paragraph: morphisms and functoriality

proof.text: If $\Lambda$ is commutative, part 2 of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-transport] applies, since $F$ is braided by [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point], part 4. In the present notation its compatibility with the braiding says $\delta_{\Lambda,\Lambda}\circ\beta_{F\Lambda,F\Lambda}=F(\beta_{\Lambda,\Lambda})\circ\delta_{\Lambda,\Lambda}$. Consequently $\mu_X\circ\beta_{F\Lambda,F\Lambda}=F(\mu)\circ F(\beta_{\Lambda,\Lambda})\circ\delta_{\Lambda,\Lambda}=F(\mu\circ\beta_{\Lambda,\Lambda})\circ\delta_{\Lambda,\Lambda}=F(\mu)\circ\delta_{\Lambda,\Lambda}=\mu_X$. This proves commutativity for the specified ring object.

source.place: proof, second paragraph: preservation of commutativity
